interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve an authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window, or publication status.
sourcePolicy: Department of Pharmaceuticals Gazette notifications, guidelines and official reports only; third-party claims are excluded.

records.sourceAnchor: Sections 2-13 and Annexures B-C: objective, 41 products, incentive rates, greenfield condition, thresholds, tenure and application route
observations: The Gazette describes a PLI scheme for 41 identified KSM/DI/API products covering 53 APIs, applicable only to greenfield projects and Indian-registered manufacturers.
The Gazette records product-specific incentive rates and a six-year sales-based incentive period, with a scheme tenure of FY 2020-21 to FY 2029-30 and a 120-day application window.
The record must separate the selected-manufacturer incentive from any general startup/MSME grant or loan and must not imply that an open application window still exists.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm whether any amendment, extension, selected-participant clarification or claim/disbursement notice changes the historical window or current status.
Validate all 41 product mappings, threshold-investment values, sales calculations, statutory-auditor evidence and disbursement conditions.
Mark the opportunity as historical/closed if the current official source set confirms that no new applications are open.

supportingSources.anchor: Official list of approved PLI Pharmaceuticals applications by Group A, B and C

records.sourceAnchor: Sections 2, 3.1 and 3.2; objective, target groups and scheme outlay
observations: The Gazette defines Group A, B and C applicant bands using FY 2019-20 global manufacturing revenue of pharmaceutical goods, with a separate MSME sub-group within Group C.

The Gazette describes a ₹15,000 crore total scheme allocation and an incentive model for selected manufacturers of specified pharmaceutical goods; this is not a universal benefit for every pharma business.
The official approved-applications document demonstrates that selection is participant-specific and must not be represented as automatic eligibility.
reviewFollowUps: Reconcile the Gazette with the 1 June 2021 guidelines and any later amendments, approved-participant notices, claim periods or scheme closure notices.
Verify target product categories, group thresholds, investment/sales requirements, applicant obligations and disbursement conditions from the complete current guideline.
Determine whether the user-facing record should be an historical selected-participant opportunity, a closed scheme reference, or a current route with a verified open window.

supportingSources.anchor: Section 5.17.1: PLI Medical Devices, revised guidelines, target segments, incentive rate and approved applicants

records.sourceAnchor: Pages 1-10 and target-segment/claim provisions: applicant, greenfield project, four target segments, incentive calculation and disbursement
observations: Official DoP material describes four target segments: cancer care/radiotherapy; radiology, imaging and nuclear imaging; anaesthetics/cardio-respiratory and renal care; and implants including implantable electronic devices.
The official report describes a 5% incremental-sales incentive for selected applicants, with Category A and Category B applicant caps and a scheme tenure through FY 2027-28.
The record must distinguish selected-participant claims from an open application opportunity and preserve the revised guideline version history.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm that the cited February 2023 document is the current operative guideline and reconcile it with the August 2022 revision and any later notices.
Validate applicant categories, investment thresholds, product list, incremental-sales calculation, claims, caps and disbursement conditions.
Confirm whether new applications are closed and expose the historical/selected-participant status if no current window exists.

supportingSources.anchor: Sections 1-4: objective, common infrastructure, State proposer, four parks, ₹400 crore outlay and ₹100 crore per park limit

records.sourceAnchor: Pages 1-8, Sections 3-8: park definition, State proposer, scope, grant limits, selection and implementation
observations: The guideline describes a Central Sector infrastructure scheme in which a State Government is the proposer and common infrastructure facilities are created for medical-device parks.
The guideline states a ₹400 crore total outlay, support for four parks, and a maximum ₹100 crore grant-in-aid per park.
The guideline states a FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25 duration, so this record is presumptively historical/closed unless a later official extension or successor route is found.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm whether any official extension, successor scheme, final sanction or closure notice changes the FY 2024-25 boundary.
Keep State proposer, selected-park and common-infrastructure benefits separate from direct founder/manufacturer assistance.
Record the four supported State/park outcomes and current access route only if supported by current official evidence; otherwise archive as historical reference.
